answer: The admission bond is a staking derivative covered by an insurance policy that pays out on wrongful slashing but not on proven fraud, so a convicted farm loses its bond and its cover. A farm must buy a thousand policies and lose them all on conviction, while one honest agent's policy never pays because it is never slashed. The cipher of the design is public, the copper of stakes makes farming a losing trade, and the raven of honest work is what finally pays.
